headline: Cricket at Asian Games kicks off September 17, featuring 12 nations
summary: The Asian Games cricket tournament begins on September 17, featuring both men's and women's events. Twelve nations, including cricketing powerhouses like Bangladesh and India, will compete for gold in Japan.
details: The Asian Games officially open on September 19, but cricket action begins earlier. Asian cricketing powerhouses will compete for gold, including full ICC member teams like Bangladesh, India, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka, alongside host Japan and other nations.

Cricket is making its fourth appearance at the Asian Games in 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, having previously been included in Guangzhou 2010, Incheon 2014, and Hangzhou 2023. This year's event features two categories: men's and women's.

A total of 12 countries are participating in cricket. The men's event features 10 teams, while the women's event has 8 teams. Bangladesh, India, Japan, Malaysia, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka have teams in both categories.

The women's tournament starts on September 17, with the gold and bronze medal matches scheduled for September 22. The men's competition begins on September 24, with medal matches taking place on October 3.

All cricket matches will be held at Kurogi Sports Park, which has a spectator capacity of 2,000. This venue previously hosted the East Asia-Pacific Sub-Regional Qualifier for the 2026 T20 World Cup earlier this year.

In the women's event, full ICC members Bangladesh, India, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka qualified directly, with Japan as the host. Malaysia, Thailand, and China secured their spots through a qualifying tournament. Quarter-final matchups include Bangladesh vs China and India vs Japan.

For the men's event, 10 teams are participating. India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, and Bangladesh, being higher-ranked ICC full members, will directly play in the quarter-finals. The remaining six teams are divided into two preliminary groups, with the top two from each group advancing to the quarter-finals.
Both men's and women's teams from full ICC member nations have sent strong squads. Bangladesh's women's team includes Nigar Sultana and Marufa Akter, while the men's team is captained by Liton Das.

India is considered the favourite for gold in both categories. Their men's team, fresh off an Asia Cup victory, features players like Shreyas Iyer and Sanju Samson, while Harmanpreet Kaur and Smriti Mandhana lead their women's side.

headline: Man Utd crash out of League Cup after blowing 2-goal lead against Brighton
summary: Manchester United suffered a stunning 3-2 defeat to Brighton, exiting the League Cup after conceding three goals in the second half despite an early two-goal lead.
details: Manchester United's problems mounted as they crashed out of the League Cup, suffering a stunning 3-2 defeat against Brighton. The Red Devils blew a two-goal lead at Old Trafford, marking their second successive home defeat.
United initially took a commanding lead with goals from Shea Lacey and Mason Mount within the first 10 minutes of the match, setting a promising tone for their League Cup campaign.

However, Brighton staged a remarkable comeback. Charalampos Kostoulas initiated their revival, followed by Pascal Gross's equalizer, and Maxim De Cuyper sealed the winner, leaving United's manager Michael Carrick shell-shocked.

This defeat adds to United's growing woes, coming just days after a controversial 1-0 home defeat against Manchester City. The club has now lost three times in six games across all competitions this season.
The result puts significant pressure on manager Michael Carrick, who was appointed permanently after leading the team to third place last season. Fans booed the team off the pitch after the collapse.
Historically, this marks the first time in 50 years that Manchester United have lost a home game after being two goals ahead, highlighting the severity of their current crisis.
